source.title: Provable Privacy Attacks on Trained Shallow Neural Networks
source.authors: Guy Smorodinsky; Gal Vardi; Itay Safran

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff. The source identifies itself as arXiv:2410.07632v3, dated 26 Aug 2026.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own experiments on trained networks and privacy leakage, but it does not intervene on label randomness or measure fitting random labels. It argues that the privacy implications of memorization depend on restrictive assumptions and that higher-dimensional reconstruction can be unreliable without prior knowledge; the experiments instead test membership inference.
record.gate_note: The paper's discussion that deep networks can interpolate random noise is a citation to Zhang et al. (2016), not a result of this study. Its experiments report trained-model membership inference behavior, so those results bear on none of V1–V6. No rows for the cited random-label result.
record.test_reason: Section 2 cites Zhang et al. to justify assuming successful training and perfect classification before analyzing privacy leakage. The study neither establishes random-label fitting nor argues against any claim version. Its own results concern membership inference and reconstruction conditional on implicit-bias constraints.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish sufficient conditions for implicit-bias-driven membership inference and univariate candidate-set reconstruction, and report empirical membership-inference behavior beyond the theoretical regime. These conclusions do not test random-label fitting.
record.recipe_differences: Studies membership inference and data reconstruction based on implicit-bias constraints for two-layer ReLU networks; it does not reproduce random-label memorization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Membership-inference behavior varies with input dimension, proximity to a KKT point, dataset/architecture, and the fraction of training and test samples at or above the margin. The reported experiments describe these trends, but their plot-only values are not extracted as rows because none tests the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 3.2 establishes separation between training and fresh-point output magnitudes under KKT and near-orthogonality assumptions, for arbitrary label assignments. Successful fitting is assumed rather than proved.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Implicit-bias constraints enable membership inference for two-layer ReLU networks under sufficient data-separation assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.2 reports perfect training accuracy and at least 85% test accuracy on Gaussian-mixture classification data. Section 3.2 and Appendix E examine membership-inference indicators across dimension, architecture, training epochs, and width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin-based membership-inference behavior can persist beyond the theoretical regime and varies with dimension and training progress.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4.4 constructs a finite candidate set containing at least one-quarter training points under univariate KKT, local-optimality, and always-active-neuron assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training points can be partially reconstructed from certain trained univariate two-layer ReLU networks.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says the code is available here but supplies no URL)
record.problems: The experiments are described as qualitative exploration beyond the theory's regime, not validation of its guarantees there. Figures report averages over 10 runs and are not accompanied by uncertainty intervals in the supplied text. The main theoretical membership-inference result depends on near-orthogonality and an implicit-bias/KKT assumption; univariate reconstruction additionally requires local optimality and an always-active neuron.
record.rows_left_out: No results bear on V1–V6, so no rows are included. The paper's experiments in Sections 3.2 and Appendix E concern margin-based membership inference, not random-label fitting. Their values are presented in figures, and are summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Random-label training accuracy, chance test accuracy, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or unstructured Gaussian-noise inputs. The Gaussian-mixture classification experiments do not measure this.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test performance across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels. The training-epoch experiment measures membership-inference indicators instead.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T5 classification. Arbitrary-label applicability of a theorem conditional on successful fitting does not establish that training reaches such a solution. No claim-version rows or verdicts are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not train on random labels or report training and test error under random labeling.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across label corruption levels.
No experiments on shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep over the fraction of randomly corrupted labels or corresponding training and test error.
No intervention on weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation in random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
No comparison of learning order or patterns learned for real versus noisy or random labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
